Before You Ask
## The questions we get most.
If yours is further out, ask us directly and we answer today.
What areas do you serve?
We cover the whole Dallas-Fort Worth Metroplex: Dallas, Fort Worth, Arlington, Plano, Frisco, Irving, Southlake, Grapevine, McKinney, Denton, Richardson and the mid-cities, roughly forty miles out from our base in ZIP 76053. Further out is usually still possible; ask us with the venue address and we will tell you straight away.
What is included in a DJ booking?
The DJ, the sound system, the microphones and the dance-floor lighting, delivered, set up, line-checked and run by our technician from load-in to breakdown. The person and the gear come together, on one booking. The detail is on the DJ services page.
Do you rent equipment without a DJ?
Yes. If you have already hired your DJ, or the host is running the music themselves, we supply the rig on its own: media players, mixer, controller, DJ booth, speakers and subwoofers. It still arrives delivered, built and line-checked by our technician rather than handed over at a counter. See DJ equipment rental .
Do you offer DJ equipment rental in Dallas?
We do, across the whole Metroplex. DJ equipment rental with us means the gear is delivered, set up, sound checked with your DJ and picked up after the event. Our crew brings it in, rigs it, tests it and comes back for it at the end of the night. Full list of what you can rent is on the DJ equipment rental page, and the wider audio inventory is on sound equipment rental .
How far in advance should I book?
Peak Saturdays in spring and autumn go early, so six to nine months out is comfortable for a wedding and three months for most corporate dates. That said, we keep inventory for short notice more often than people expect, so if your date is close, ask anyway.
Do you provide lighting and uplighting separately?
Yes. Uplighting , dance-floor and stage lighting, monograms, pin spots and lasers can be booked on their own or added to an audio booking, which is the more common route because it means one crew and one load-in. The hub is lighting services .
What is Dancing on the Clouds?
A low-lying fog effect for a first dance or a grand entrance. The fog sits at ankle height instead of filling the room, so the couple appears to be standing on a cloud and the photographs come out beautifully. Details on the Dancing on the Clouds page.
How do I get a quote?
Tell us the date, the venue and roughly how many guests, and we will come back with a straightforward quote. Tell us about your event and you'll hear back from us today, with a straightforward quote within 24 hours. Contact us here or call 817-210-7957.
What does AV equipment rental include?
Delivery, setup, a line check and breakdown at the end, with an insured AV technician on site for the whole event on the services that call for one and whenever you ask. An AV rental from us is sound, lighting, projection and effects specified as one system rather than as separate line items, and when a technician stays, the same person who sets it up is the one running it when your first speaker walks up. Start on the sound equipment rental page and we will fill in the rest around your room.
Do you handle AV for corporate events and conferences?
Yes. Conferences, general sessions, awards nights, panels, product launches and multi-day meetings. That usually means a sound system sized to the room, presenter and lapel microphones carrying our De-Feedback system, projection and screens bright enough for the actual light in the room, and stage lighting, all from one crew and one load-in. The corporate events page has the detail.

Ceremony Sound Rentals
## Every word of the vows, heard from the back row the first time.
A ceremony is quiet voices, an outdoor space with open air on every side, and one take, and we plan it that way. At a recent outdoor ceremony in Dallas-Fort Worth that meant two lapel microphones running our AI-powered De-Feedback system, two EV ZLX speakers placed for the rows of chairs, and a condenser microphone over the string quartet so the prelude reached the last row as clearly as the first.
1
Everyone hears it, including the back row. Speakers placed for the seating plan you have, so the last row hears the vows as clearly as the first. Outdoors we plan for wind and open air; indoors we tune to the room so every word stays intelligible at a comfortable level.
2
Wireless handheld and lapel mics, with AI De-Feedback standard. Every wireless microphone rental includes our AI-powered feedback-suppression system as standard. The officiant, the readings and the vows all come through clean.
3
Live musicians get their own inputs. A string trio, a solo guitarist, a harpist, a vocalist. We mic and reinforce them properly instead of hoping a laptop speaker carries it, and we run the balance live as the processional starts.
4
Cues are run by a person at the board. Our ceremony audio engineer is there for the processional, the pause, the kiss, and the recessional. If the wedding party is thirty seconds late, the music waits with them.
5
Then it moves to the reception. The same team strikes the ceremony rig and has cocktail hour and the reception up before your guests find their seats.

Common Questions
## Wedding AV questions, answered straight.
What is included in a rental?
We deliver, set up, test and pick up everything ourselves, and we run every cable. Who stays on site depends on what you book. Our DJ packages include your DJ and sound engineer on site for the event. A ceremony-only booking includes a ceremony audio engineer for one hour, so the ceremony sounds right. For a traveling DJ or wedding band, we set up, sound check with the musicians and pick everything up after the send off. Your wedding party gets to enjoy the day.
Can you cover an outdoor ceremony with no power?
Yes. Outdoor ceremonies are routine for us. We plan for the distance, the wind, and the power situation ahead of time, including battery-powered options where there's no outlet. Tell us where the aisle is and we'll tell you what it takes.
What about microphone feedback during the vows and toasts?
Every microphone rental includes our AI-powered De-Feedback system as standard. It suppresses feedback before it becomes the squeal everyone remembers, which matters most in the two moments you can't redo: the vows and the toasts.
We're bringing our own DJ or band. Can you just provide the gear?
That's a big part of what we do. Traveling wedding DJs get CDJs, mixers, PA, subs, booth and facade; live wedding bands get front-of-house, monitors, subs, stands, cables, and a console on request. It's all set up and line-checked, we sound check it with your DJ or band before guests arrive, and we pick it up after the send off. Your DJ or band walks into a working system.
How far in advance should we book?
Peak DFW wedding dates, spring and fall Saturdays, get claimed first, often a year out. If you have a date and a venue, send them over and we'll tell you honestly whether we're open. If we're not, we'll say so rather than stringing you along.
Do you handle the ceremony and the reception, or just one?
Either, but most couples book both. It's one delivery, one setup crew, and one point of contact instead of coordinating two vendors across the same afternoon. We strike the ceremony rig and have cocktail hour and the reception up while your guests are still finding their tables.
Wedding service area: Dallas, Fort Worth, McKinney, Richardson, Southlake, Rockwall, Frisco, Waxahachie, Arlington, Plano, Denton, and the wider Metroplex. Getting married outside that ring? Ask us . We travel for the right event.

Ceremony
## Ceremony sound, including the weddings with no DJ at all
Rig Officiant microphone · optional second microphone for the vows · speakers placed for the seating · music playback
A wedding ceremony sound system rental is a small job with the whole room listening. The vows are the quietest thing that happens all day, they happen once, and half the guests are behind a row of hats. We size the speakers to the seating rather than to the room, place them where the aisle photograph stays clean, and set levels with someone standing where the officiant will stand. Music playback for the processional and the recessional runs from the same system, so the walk in, the vows and the walk out all come off one setup.
A growing number of the ceremonies we cover have a string quartet, a harpist or a guitarist playing instead of a DJ. Live musicians are the reason to call an audio company rather than a DJ company. A quartet in a garden or a stone chapel needs to be reinforced so it still sounds like a quartet in a garden, and the officiant still needs a wireless microphone over the top of it. That is a mix, and somebody has to be there making it.
Every wireless microphone we send out runs our AI-powered De-Feedback system, which buys real gain before feedback. That matters most outdoors and in stone or glass rooms, where the microphone has to be turned up to be heard over the wind or the reverb and that is when it wants to ring. A second wireless microphone for the vows is optional, and it is the add on we suggest most often, because vows spoken toward each other are quieter than anything else on the schedule.

## Wedding AV rental questions
We have a string quartet at the ceremony instead of a DJ. What do we need?
A ceremony system and someone mixing it. A string quartet in a garden, a courtyard or a stone chapel usually needs light reinforcement so the back rows hear it, and the officiant needs a wireless microphone sitting over the top of that without either one fighting the other. We size the speakers to the seating, place them out of the aisle photograph, and set levels with a person standing where the officiant will stand. Wireless microphones run our AI-powered De-Feedback system, which gives real gain before feedback outdoors and in reverberant rooms. Music playback for the processional and the recessional comes from the same system, and a second wireless microphone for the vows is optional.
Our band is flying in. Can you provide the PA and backline in Dallas?
Yes, and we get that call most weeks. Send us the stage plot and the input list and we quote front of house, monitors, microphones, direct boxes and backline together. Everything is standing at the venue and tested before the band arrives, then sound checked with the band by the crew that patched it, and we pick it all up after the send off. Bands that travel without their own engineer can add ours, who sets the microphone levels, runs a real sound check while the room is empty and stays on the console through the set.
Our DJ is traveling and only brings a controller. Can he plug into your system?
Yes. We set the whole front of house before he lands: speakers on stands, subwoofers for the dance floor, a booth at working height, power and balanced inputs ready for his controller. He plugs in, sets his levels and plays. We can also cover the ceremony an hour earlier and hand a checked system across for the reception, which is what usually happens when there is live music at the ceremony and a DJ at the reception.
What is included in a rental?
We deliver, set up, test and collect. Delivery, setup, testing and breakdown are included in every booking, and we handle the transport both ways. Our crew has the system placed, patched and tested before guests arrive, sound checks it with your DJ or band, and comes back to load it out after the send off. The exception is a ceremony where we run the audio: our engineer stays through the ceremony and mixes it live. TVs, projectors, lighting and a mixer with Bluetooth for couples playing their own music are set up, tested and picked up. Your wedding party never carries a speaker or coils a cable.
Can we rent sound equipment for our wedding and play our own music?
Yes. Our wedding sound equipment rental covers speakers placed for the seating, a mixer with Bluetooth for your playlist and wireless microphones for the toasts and the ceremony. We drop it off, set it up, test it with your phone or tablet before guests arrive and pick it up after the send off. If you want the ceremony mixed live, add our ceremony audio engineer.
Can you run a photo slideshow at the reception?
Yes. We bring the projector, the screen and the playback, or televisions on floor stands where a screen would look wrong. Wedding venues are lit for photography and rarely go dark, so we usually recommend an ambient light rejecting screen or an ultra short throw projector that guests cannot walk in front of. Send us the room and the length of the montage and we will tell you which one fits.
Can we add uplighting and a monogram to the same booking?
Yes, and it is the reason to book audio, video and lighting in one place. Wireless battery uplights go around the room in your color with no cable taped across the floor, and a monogram with your names, initials or date is projected onto a wall, a dance floor or the ceiling. Do you work with our wedding planner and our venue directly?
Yes, and planners are a large part of who we work for. Planners who book us repeatedly do it because the AV is one vendor, one arrival and one contact instead of three.
How far ahead should we book wedding AV in Dallas-Fort Worth?
As soon as you have a date and a venue, especially for Saturdays between March and June and again in October and November. That said, we take short notice weddings and we would rather you asked than assumed. Tell us the date, the venue and the guest count and we will tell you today whether the day is open.

### Sound and microphones
Speech is the entire product at a corporate event, so corporate event audio is built around it. Wireless handhelds, lavaliers, podium and tabletop microphones , PA sized and aimed for the room, and a mixer run by a person rather than left on a preset. Every microphone carries our AI-powered De-Feedback system as standard, which catches the ring before a room full of people hears it.
Why it matters If the back row cannot hear the speaker, nothing else on this page counts.
02 · Video

Projectors and screens sized to the throw and the ambient light, TVs for breakouts and lobbies , confidence monitors so the presenter faces the room, and a switcher between the laptops so slide changes and speaker changes happen with the big screen showing only slides. See projector & screen rental for the equipment side.
Why it matters Someone will hand you a laptop five minutes before doors. We plan for that.
03 · Lighting

Front light so faces read on camera and from the back of the room, uplighting to bring a flat ballroom up to the brand, a follow spot for award presentations, and logo or monogram projection where it makes sense. Our lighting services run on the same crew and the same load-in as the audio and video.

Multi-camera live streaming to the platform your company already uses, with the audio patched directly from our mixer rather than picked up by a camera mic, so remote attendees hear the same processed, De-Feedback’d speech the room hears. AV Production, In Plain English
## What “AV production” covers.
It is a phrase every company uses and each one means something different by it. When we quote AV production for a corporate event, this is what is inside it: four jobs, and every one of them happens on every event.
### 01. Planning the room before anyone is in it
Reading the floor plan and the run of show, working out where the system has to go so that sightlines, coverage and cable runs all survive contact with the actual venue, and agreeing a load-in window with whoever owns the loading dock. This is the part that decides whether event day is calm.
### 02. Building and testing the system
Rigging and cabling the audio, video and lighting, powering it in a way the venue’s circuits can support, then line-checking every input (every microphone, every laptop, every playback source) long before the first person walks in.
### 03. Operating it live
A technician on the console for the whole event, riding levels as speakers change, cutting between sources, catching the lapel that needs re-clipping, and handling the five minutes of the schedule that always change on the day.
### 04. Getting out cleanly
Striking the system quietly while guests are still finishing their drinks, and taking every case out on our truck so your team walks out with empty hands.
Event Technology Services
## Event technology, run by the people who installed it that morning.
Event technology services is the broader version of the same job: everything in the room that has to be powered, connected and working at a specific minute. Presentation switching and slide advance, confidence monitors, hybrid connections for remote presenters, wired and wireless audio distribution, video record feeds, and the network-dependent pieces that quietly decide whether a remote panelist joins on time.
The difference between event technology that works and event technology that becomes the story of the day is rarely the equipment. It is whether the person who built the system is still in the room when something changes, and at a real corporate event, something always changes. A speaker arrives with a different deck. A panel moves from four chairs to five. The keynote runs eleven minutes long and the breakouts have to absorb it.
We staff for that, and it is what AV support for corporate events means to us. The technician who loads in is the technician at the console, so the setup lives in one head all day.

Corporate AV FAQ
## The questions planners ask.
If yours is missing, send it with your inquiry. We would rather answer it before the quote than after.
Are you an audio visual company or an equipment rental company?
Both, but in that order. Dallas Event Audio is a full-service audio visual company serving Dallas-Fort Worth: we specify, deliver, install and operate complete AV systems for corporate events. Equipment rental is part of that. Every rental is delivered, set up, tested and picked up by our crew, and for corporate events an on-site technician stays to run it, because that is what makes the room work.
What corporate AV services do you offer?
Sound systems and microphones, projection, screens, displays and confidence monitors, presentation switching, stage and room lighting, follow spot and logo projection, live streaming and hybrid connections, recording, DJ services, and the technicians to run all of it. For most corporate events these are quoted together as one production rather than as separate rentals.
Do you provide on-site technicians?
Yes, on every corporate event. Each system arrives with the technician who runs it. Our crew loads in, builds and line-checks the system, runs rehearsal with your speakers, operates sound, video and lighting for the whole event, and strikes afterwards. The technician who built the system is the one at the console, so the setup stays in one head all day.
What does AV production mean for a corporate event?
In practice it means four things: planning the room before anyone is in it, building and testing the system, operating it live as the schedule changes, and striking it cleanly at the end. Equipment is only one input to that. When we quote AV production we are quoting all four, which is why the number covers a working room rather than a list of gear.
Can you handle a large conference end to end, general session and breakouts?
Yes, end to end. General sessions are a regular part of what we do: line array or point-source sound scaled to the depth of the room, large-format projection, stage and podium lighting, presentation switching, and front-of-house operation for the duration. Multi-room conferences with breakouts running alongside the main room are quoted as a single production with one crew and one schedule, from the advance call through load-out.
Do you cover keynote AV and breakout room AV with the same crew?
Yes. We treat the keynote room and the breakout rooms as a single production. The same crew builds the general session and every breakout in one load-in, labels each room to its own schedule, and covers them through the day, which is what keeps a session change on time when a breakout runs long.
Do you offer live streaming and hybrid support?
Yes, and the audio is the part that makes it worth doing properly. We patch the stream feed directly from our mixer rather than relying on a camera microphone, so remote attendees hear the same processed, De-Feedback’d speech as the room. Multi-camera setups, remote presenter connections and recording are all available. There is more detail on the live streaming page.
Do we have to use the venue’s in-house AV?
Usually you can bring us in. Most hotels and conference centers in Dallas-Fort Worth allow outside AV vendors, and many that restrict certain elements still allow the rest. Send us the venue name with your inquiry and we will confirm their policy before you commit to anything, then deal with their operations team on load-in, dock access and paperwork directly.
Are you insured? Can you provide a COI for our venue?
Yes. We are fully insured and routinely provide certificates of insurance naming the venue as required. Send us the venue’s requirements with your booking and we will have the certificate issued and sent to them directly, well ahead of your load-in date.
Can you support a recurring meeting series?
Yes, and it is some of our favorite work. Quarterly all-hands, monthly trainings, annual kickoffs and recurring board meetings all get easier once the room is documented: power, acoustics, load-in timing, what the house system can be trusted with. You can book event by event or set us up as a standing AV partner for the series; either way the same crew comes back.
What areas do you serve?
Dallas, Fort Worth and the surrounding Metroplex, roughly a forty-mile radius from our base in the mid-cities, which covers Dallas, Fort Worth, Irving, Plano, Frisco, Arlington, Grapevine, Southlake, Las Colinas, Addison, Richardson and the rest of the mid-cities. Events further out are possible; ask us when you send your date.
How far in advance should we book?
Earlier is better, particularly for conference season and December, and a late call is still a welcome call. Short-notice bookings are often workable. What helps most is sending the run of show and the venue as early as you have them, because the advance work is where most event-day problems get solved.
How do we get a quote?
Send the date, the venue, the room or rooms, roughly how many people and what has to happen: presentations, panels, awards, a stream, a party afterwards. ## Party speaker rental sized to the room and the guest count
The question people ask first is how many speakers a party needs. The better question is what the room does to sound and where the guests will be standing when it matters. A living room, a hotel ballroom and a back yard with a pool between the bar and the dance floor are three different problems, and the answer is a coverage plan rather than a quantity. Rig BassBoss subwoofers · paired with the main speakers

Rig Shure wireless handheld · lapel available · AI-powered De-Feedback

Lighting
## Party lighting rental and dance floor lighting
Lighting is what makes a room read as a party rather than as a rented space with music in it. Uplighting around the walls sets the color of the whole evening and photographs better than anything else you can add for the money. Dance floor lighting gives the floor a reason to fill once the room goes dark.

Questions
## Private party sound and lighting questions
Can I rent speakers for a party in Dallas?
Yes, and the rental comes with a professional crew. We deliver the speakers, place them for the room, tune and test them before guests arrive, and come back to take everything away at the end. An AV technician can stay to run the system through the party if you would like one. Tell us the venue or address, the guest count and whether there will be dancing, and we will tell you what the space needs.
How many speakers does a party need?
It depends on the shape of the room and where guests will be standing rather than on a headcount alone. A long narrow space needs coverage down its length, an open back yard has no walls helping the sound along, and a room with a separate bar and dance area needs both covered. Send us the venue or the address and we will plan the coverage and quote it.
Do you provide a microphone for toasts and speeches?
Yes. Wireless handheld microphones are part of most private event setups, with lapel microphones available when somebody needs their hands free. All of our wireless runs an AI-powered De-Feedback system, so the person speaking can move toward the guests without the squeal that usually cuts a speech short. Batteries are changed on our schedule rather than when they die.
Do you set up backyard and house parties?
Often. At a house the limits are power, neighbors and the distance the sound has to travel, so we walk the property or the plan in advance, aim the coverage inward toward where guests gather, confirm the circuits we can use and route cable where nobody will trip on it after dark. Outdoor coverage is a placement problem rather than a volume problem.
Can you do the lighting and the DJ as well as the sound?
Yes, and it is one quote and one crew. Party lighting, uplighting, dance floor lighting, a DJ, projectors and screens and event photo and video all get booked together as one audio visual package and set up on the same visit. That is the reason to use one company for a private event instead of coordinating three that have never worked together.
How far in advance should I book a graduation party?
Earlier than feels necessary. May and June fill first because every high school and college in the Metroplex graduates in the same few weeks, and the good dates go months ahead. Holiday parties in December behave the same way. For everything else a few weeks is usually enough, and we will always tell you honestly if a date is still open.
Do you cover galas and fundraisers?
Yes. A gala runs on its program, so we treat the podium, the wireless handhelds, the video playback and the screens as one system, and we recommend an AV technician on it the whole night. We set the podium microphone level with a person standing at it, take the video audio as a source instead of pointing a microphone at a laptop, and keep a spare microphone live for the auction.
What areas around Dallas do you serve?
The Dallas-Fort Worth Metroplex, roughly a 40 mile radius from ZIP 76053. That includes Dallas, Fort Worth, Plano, Frisco, Arlington, Irving, McKinney, Denton, Grapevine, Southlake and the surrounding cities. If your venue is further out, ask anyway and we will tell you honestly whether it works.

How It Works
## One company for the audio, the lighting and the stage
A live show has more moving parts than any other kind of event we run. There is a stage plot, an input list, a soundcheck window that is always shorter than everyone hoped, and a room that behaves differently once it is full. Live event production is the work of getting all of that to land at the same time.
Our live event services for bands all work the same way: every band booking is a full service rental. Our crew delivers the system, builds it for the room, tunes it to the room, mixes the show live and strikes it at the end of the night. The people running the console are ours, and the whole rig goes back out on our truck.
Audio, lighting and DJ support come from the same company on one quote and one load in, which is the difference between a show that soundchecks on time and three vendors introducing themselves in a loading dock at four in the afternoon.

Live Audio
## Live sound services for bands, concerts and venues
Once a band is playing, the speaker package becomes an input list and a room to cover from it. Here is what our live event audio setup is made of, all professional grade gear from our own inventory and all of it run by our engineer.
01
### Front of house sound for the room
Rig Tops on sticks or an array on stands · subwoofers · fills
Coverage comes first. A club room takes a pair of tops and subs, while a deep hall or an outdoor lot needs a line array speaker system so the back of the crowd hears the same mix as the front. Subwoofers go in for kick and bass guitar rather than for volume, and fills cover the seats beyond the main hangs.
02
### Stage monitors and in-ear support
Rig Wedge monitors · separate mixes · in-ear patching
Bands play to what they hear on stage, so monitoring is the part that decides whether the performance is comfortable. We build separate mixes for vocals, drums and the players who need to hear each other, and we patch in-ear systems where the band already travels with them. More mixes means a longer line check, which is why we ask for the stage plot early.
03
### The input list: drums, amps, instruments, vocals
Rig Full band microphone package · DI boxes · stands
Kick, snare, overheads, guitar and bass cabinets, keys and acoustic instruments on DI, and a vocal microphone for every singer plus one for whoever talks between songs. Our microphone rentals run an AI-powered De-Feedback system, which matters most on a small stage where a vocal mic is a few feet from a wedge. The De-Feedback explainer covers how it works.
04
### Console and an engineer who stays
Rig Digital console · on site audio engineer · full show
A live mix moves. The room absorbs high end as it fills, the singer works the microphone differently in the second set, and the guitar player turns up. Our engineer is on the console for the whole show, holds the level where the room and the venue can take it, and deals with a dead channel before the audience notices it.
05
### Backline and stage gear
Rig Drum riser support · stands · cabling · power on stage
We carry the stage side pieces a show needs around the band's own instruments: stands, DI boxes, cabling, power distribution on the deck and the small parts that go missing at nine at night. If your show needs full backline such as a house drum kit or specific amplifiers, tell us in the advance and we will say honestly what we carry and what we would bring in.
06
### Multi band nights and changeovers
Rig Shared input list · line checks between sets
Three bands on a bill is three input lists sharing one stage. We build the patch so the common channels stay put, line check the differences between sets, and keep the changeover to the length of the break rather than the length of a full setup. Send the running order with the stage plots and we will plan it around the doors time.
### Not sure what the room needs?
Send us the venue or the address, the expected head count and the stage plot if you have one. We will tell you what the space calls for and quote it. The sound system rental page has the wider inventory and audio services covers the rest of what we run.

Stage Lighting
## Stage lighting for a live performance
Lighting is what makes a band look like a show rather than a rehearsal. Front light so faces read from the back of the room, color washes across the stage, moving heads and effects for the parts of the set that want them, and haze so the beams have shape in the air. We program it to the set list where we have one, so the hits land on the beat all night.
The lighting plot gets built around the stage rather than dropped on top of it. Where the fixtures hang or stand, where the power comes from and how the cable runs across the deck are worked out alongside the speaker positions, so the lighting and the audio each have their own piece of ceiling on the day.
Small rooms get a front wash, a few movers and haze. A festival stage or a ticketed show gets a real plot with washes, beams, backlight and effects cued to the set. Either way it is quoted on the same job as the audio and built on the same load in by the same crew. Event lighting has the full picture, and uplighting covers the room around the stage.

## Live music and band AV questions
Who provides staging, lighting and sound for live events in Dallas?
Dallas Event Audio has been doing it across the Dallas-Fort Worth Metroplex since 2001. We supply the front of house sound, the stage monitoring, the microphones and the stage lighting on one quote, and our crew delivers it, builds it, mixes the show and loads it out. Where a show needs physical staging such as risers or decking, we advance that with a staging vendor so both plans match. Send us the date and the venue and we will quote it.
Do you provide the sound system and an engineer, or just the equipment?
Both together, always. Every live event audio booking is full service, so the system arrives with our crew, gets built and tuned for the room, and an engineer stays on the console for the whole show. We do not drop equipment off for a band to run on its own, which is what keeps a live mix consistent from the first song to the last.
What do you need from the band before the show?
A stage plot and an input list if the band has them, plus the running order when there is more than one act. That tells us the channel count, how many monitor mixes to build and where everything sits on the deck. If the band does not have either, describe the lineup and the instruments and we will write the input list for you.
Can you cover a venue that already has a house sound system?
Often, yes. Many rooms have a system specified for background music that runs out of headroom the moment a full band plugs in. We either supplement it with subwoofers, monitors and microphones, or bring a complete system in for the night and leave the house rig alone. We advance it with the venue's own staff so the circuits, the rigging points and the load in window are settled before doors.
How many microphones does a live band need?
A four piece with vocals is usually somewhere between ten and sixteen channels once the drum kit, the cabinets, the acoustic instruments on DI and every singer are counted. Add a channel for whoever talks between songs. Our microphones run an AI-powered De-Feedback system, which matters most on a small stage where the vocal microphones sit a few feet in front of a monitor wedge.
Do you handle multi band bills and changeovers?
Yes, and it is mostly a planning job. We build the patch around the channels every act shares, line check only the differences between sets, and keep the changeover inside the length of the break. Send the running order with each band's stage plot and we will build the schedule backward from doors.
Can you do an outdoor concert or a festival stage?
Yes. Outdoors the coverage has to come from placement and array design rather than from volume, so we plan the throw for where the crowd will stand, keep the level off the property line where a permit requires it, and confirm the power path and weather cover in the advance. Tell us the site and the expected head count and we will size the system for it.

Game Day
## Tailgate party sound systems and DJs
A tailgate party is an outdoor event with open air on every side, a hard start time tied to kickoff, and a crowd that moves around instead of sitting down. The sound has to carry across a lot and still be clean by the time it reaches the row of cars three deep, and it has to survive being outdoors in Texas in September.
We build tailgate party sound around coverage rather than raw volume. Speakers on poles at the height of the crowd, aimed into the space the crowd is standing in, with subwoofers on the ground so the music has weight while the tops stay clean. If the lot needs its own power we plan for that in the advance rather than at nine in the morning on game day.
Add a DJ and the tailgate runs itself. Our DJ handles the music, the announcements and the volume across the whole window, drops the level when the band or the pep squad comes through, and brings it back up after. A wireless handheld goes in the kit so whoever is welcoming alumni or running the raffle is heard over an open parking lot.

The gala on this page, with the monogram over a full floor and the uplighting running the walls, was one of those rooms, and the outdoor stage with the vendor tents was the other end of the same year.
### Graduation ceremonies and awards nightsProcessional playback, podium mics, name reading, outdoor coverage
Graduation is a long form event where the only thing anyone remembers is whether they could hear their own kid's name. That puts everything on the podium microphone and on coverage that reaches the last row of families in the back of a gym or the far side of a field. We handle the processional and recessional playback, the podium and the name reader, the wireless for whoever is presenting, and a screen or a stream when more people want to be there than the room can seat.
### Live bands and student ensemblesFull input list, stage monitoring, front of house
A student band, a jazz ensemble, an alumni act at a homecoming event or a headliner booked for a spring concert all need the same thing: an input list built before the day, monitors the players can work with, and a front of house engineer who has mixed a band before. Once a band is on the bill you are building an input plot rather than picking a couple of microphones, so send us the stage plot early. Our live music and band events page goes deeper on how we run those.

Bring Your Own DJ
## Sound setups for your school's own DJ
This is a common booking and it deserves saying plainly: you can hire us for the sound alone. The school books the DJ, we build the system, and the two meet at the booth. It is the same arrangement we run at weddings where the couple already has someone, and it works the same way on a campus.

School AV
## The audio we bring to campus events
All professional grade gear from our own inventory, delivered and operated by our crew. What goes on the truck depends on the room, the head count and whether anyone is speaking.
01
### Speakers for a gym, a quad or a ballroom
Rig Powered tops on poles · sized to the space
The starting point for most school events. A sound system rental built around the space you are in, on poles at crowd height and aimed at where people will be standing rather than at the back wall. Gyms are reflective and need the coverage kept tight, and outdoor lots need more boxes than the head count suggests because the sound has open air to fill.
02
### Subwoofers for a dance floor
Rig BassBoss subwoofers · ground stacked at the floor
Once there is dancing, the tops alone will run out before the room does. BassBoss subwoofers put the low end where the floor is, which lets the whole system stay clean at a level a gym full of students will call loud enough. We place them for the dance floor rather than for the stage.
03
### Line array for a big hall
Rig Line array speaker system · on stands or stacked with fills
A long auditorium or a full arena floor makes the front too loud before the back is loud enough. A line array speaker system holds the level closer to even from the first row to the last, which is what a graduation ceremony or a large university gala needs when families are seated a hundred feet apart.
04
### Wireless microphones that hold up
Rig Handheld · lapel · headset · podium · AI-powered De-Feedback
Handhelds for hosts and performers, lapel or headset for a dean or a principal who moves, and a podium microphone for the name reading. All of our wireless microphone rentals run an AI-powered De-Feedback system, so a presenter can step in front of the speakers and stay intelligible. That system comes with every microphone we send out, so the microphone is ready as soon as it is placed and stays clean once the room fills. We put fresh batteries in on our own schedule, and we set the level for every microphone with a person standing where the speaker will stand.
05
### DJ booth and playback
Rig CDJ players · mixer · booth monitor · laptop input
Whether the DJ is ours or yours, the booth is the same: CDJ players and a mixer, a monitor, and an input for a laptop or a phone when the show is running off a playlist and a running order. For talent shows we build the playback so the operator moves to the next track the moment the last act clears.
06
### A technician for the whole event
Rig On site AV technician · through setup, show and strike
Every booking includes one. They set the system, set the microphone levels at the speaking positions, hold them through the program and handle the changeovers, then strike it at the end. Our operator stands behind the mixer, and your staff and your student committee get to watch the show.
### Tell us the room and we will size it

Lighting
## Lighting for talent shows, galas and campus dance floors
School spaces are lit for classes and basketball, which is the opposite of what an event wants. Lighting is the cheapest way to make a gym stop looking like a gym, and on a stage it is the difference between an audience watching a performer and an audience watching a room.
For talent shows we light the stage so faces read from the back of the house, with a follow spot when a soloist needs to be found. For galas, uplighting around the perimeter takes a ballroom or a cafeteria into event territory, and a monogram projector puts a school seal or a class year on the wall or the dance floor. For dance nights we bring DJ lighting over the floor, with haze so the beams read and lasers where the venue allows them.
Stage wash and pin spot lighting are available as part of a larger package. Ask and we will tell you what the room can hang and what has to go on stands.

Graduation
## AV rentals for graduation ceremonies
Graduation has a fixed run of show and one job that matters more than the rest, which is that every family hears the name they came for. Here is what we plan around.
### Indoors or outWhere the ceremony happens
A gym holds sound and throws it back at you, so coverage gets aimed tight and the level stays under what the room will ring at. A field or a stadium is open on every side, so it takes more boxes spread further and a plan for power that starts weeks before the date. Tell us which one you are in and the system changes accordingly.
### The podiumName reading and speeches
The podium microphone carries the ceremony. We use a gooseneck or a wireless podium microphone with the AI-powered De-Feedback system on it, which means the microphone is ready as soon as it is placed and holds up once the room fills, set the level with somebody standing at the podium, and set a second microphone for the name reader so the reading carries on whatever happens to the first.
### MusicProcessional and recessional
Playback for the processional, the alma mater, the recessional and anything a music department is performing live. We take the running order in advance so the cues land where the program says they land, and our technician runs them rather than a volunteer with a phone.
### OverflowScreens and streaming
Most ceremonies have more family than seats. A projector and screen puts the stage in an overflow room, and live streaming sends it to grandparents who could not travel. Both get planned with the ceremony rather than bolted on the week of.

## College and school event AV questions
Do you provide sound and a DJ for a college tailgate party?
Yes, and it is a booking we take from campuses every football season. Can you run sound for a school talent show?
Yes. Send us the running order and what each act needs, and we build a playback setup that moves act to act without a gap, plus wireless microphones for the hosts and the singers. Our technician rides the levels through the whole show, so a quiet performer and a drumline both come out sounding right. Every microphone runs the AI-powered De-Feedback system, which is what lets a performer walk downstage in front of the speakers.
Do you supply the DJ, or can we use our own?
Either. We book DJs who work campus events across Dallas-Fort Worth, and plenty of schools already have a student DJ or a chapter DJ they want to use. What do you provide for a university gala?
A professional AV setup for galas covers two events in one room. For the party after you get a DJ or a feed for yours, subwoofers under the dance floor and uplighting around the room. Can you handle a graduation ceremony outdoors?
Yes. An outdoor ceremony needs more speakers spread further than the head count suggests, because there is nothing to contain the sound, and it needs the power path settled well ahead of the date. We cover the podium and the name reading with wireless microphones, run the processional and recessional playback to your running order, and can add a screen or a live stream for families who cannot be in the seats.

What is included in a campus rental?
Every campus rental is full service, so the gear is delivered, set up, tuned and operated by our crew and then loaded back out. Our crew delivers it, runs it and loads it back out. It is also why the quote is one number instead of a rental line plus a labor line.

## We bring the club with us
A rave is a room that was something else that morning. A warehouse in the Design District, a leased industrial bay off Irving Boulevard, a bar with a back room, a venue whose house system was specified for a band and gives up the moment a kick drum sits under it. The production is the event, and it arrives on a truck.
Every rave and night club event we take is a full service rental. Our crew delivers the rig, stacks or stands it where the room needs it, tunes it against the actual walls, runs it live for the length of the night and strikes it at the end. The people operating the system are ours, and every cable goes back out with us.
Audio, lighting, rave visuals and DJ service come from the same company on the same quote. One advance, one crew and one load in, instead of three vendors meeting each other in a loading dock at four in the afternoon.

Club Audio
## Club sound systems and subwoofers for a rave
Electronic music is written for a system that can reproduce the bottom two octaves at volume for six hours. That is a different specification from a party rig, and it is the part of rave audio visual production people underestimate. Below is what we build a night club sound system out of, all professional grade powered gear from our own inventory.
01
### Subwoofers built for electronic music
Rig BassBoss subwoofers · ground stacked or arrayed to the floor
The low end is the reason people came. BassBoss subwoofers hold their shape at the level a rave runs at, so a sub bass line stays a note instead of turning into pressure. We place them for the dance floor rather than for the stage, and we array them when the room is wide enough that one stack would leave a dead zone in the middle.
02
### Line array for a large room
Rig Line array speaker system · on stands or stacked with fills
Once a room is deep, point source boxes make the front too loud before the back is loud enough. A line array speaker system keeps the level closer to even from the barricade to the back wall, which is what lets you run a warehouse rave at club volume while the first thirty people still enjoy it. Fills cover the corners beyond the array.
03
### DJ booth and playback
Rig CDJ players · DJM mixer · booth monitors · facade
Guest DJs turn up with a USB stick and an expectation. We carry the Pioneer players and mixers touring DJs ask for, plus booth monitors loud enough to beatmatch against a room that is already moving, and a facade when the booth is part of how the night looks. Send us the rider and we will confirm what we have against it before the date.
04
### Power and the room
Rig Power path confirmed in advance · distro run by our crew
Warehouses and pop up venues rarely have the service a full club rig wants sitting on the wall, and finding that out at eight at night ends the night. We confirm the power path in the advance, bring distribution and run the sound, the lighting and the visuals off a plan rather than off whatever outlets are nearest.
05
### Microphones for the host
Rig Shure wireless handheld · AI-powered De-Feedback
Most of the night is music alone, and then somebody has to announce the headliner over a room at full level. Our wireless handhelds run an AI-powered De-Feedback system, so the host can walk out in front of the speakers and still be understood. Batteries are changed on our schedule rather than when they die.
06
### An engineer on it all night
Rig On site technician · levels held through every changeover
Four DJs across a night will each arrive at the mixer with different gain habits, and the room itself changes once eight hundred people are in it absorbing high end. Our technician stays with the system, catches the changeovers, keeps the level where the room can take it and deals with a dead channel before the floor notices.
### Not sure what the room needs?
Send us the venue or the address, the expected head count and the curfew. We will tell you what the space calls for and quote it. Our event audio services page covers the rest of what we run, and the sound equipment rental page has the wider inventory.
Night Types
## The rave and night club events we get called for
Every one of these is a different problem hiding behind the same words. The rig follows the room, the curfew and the crowd rather than a package name.
### Warehouse and underground ravesIndustrial space, pop up venues, one night builds
An empty warehouse has concrete on six sides, power on the far wall and a neighbor with a phone. We build the whole thing: subs on the floor, an array if the room is deep, lighting on truss or stands that we bring, and levels aimed inward so the sound in the parking lot is a fraction of the sound on the floor. We also want to know the curfew early, because load out time is part of the plan.
### Night club events and takeoversPromoter nights, brand takeovers, residencies
A club has a house system that was specified for the club's normal night. When a promoter brings in a headliner who needs more than that, we supplement rather than replace: subs added to the house rig, a booth built to the rider, lighting and rave visuals brought in for the one night and gone by morning. We advance it with the venue's staff so the circuits are settled before doors.
### EDM parties and DJ nightsHouse, techno, bass, drum and bass, open format
Genre decides the rig more than head count does. A bass night wants far more sub headroom than a house night, and an open format room wants vocals that stay intelligible over a full floor. Tell us who is playing and we will size the system for the music instead of for the square footage.
### Private rave setupsBirthdays, house parties, graduation nights that turn into a rave
A private rave setup is a real request and it books all year. Someone wants their back yard or a rented hall to feel like a club for one night: a proper sound system, lasers or moving lights, haze so the beams read, and a DJ. It is the same crew and the same gear at the scale the space can take. Our private event AV page covers the quieter version of the same booking.
### Festival stages and outdoor setsDay parties, lot shows, multi stage events
Outdoors the sound has open air to fill, so coverage comes from placement and array design rather than from turning it up. We plan the throw for where the crowd will be standing, keep sound off the property line where a permit says to, and build weather cover into the plan because a Texas afternoon does what it wants.
### After parties and late night roomsSecond rooms, conference after hours, tour after parties
A second room inside a larger event has to be loud inside and quiet outside, which is a containment problem more than a power problem. We aim the coverage tight, keep the sub energy off the shared wall where we can, and run it with somebody on the console so the level tracks what the neighboring room can tolerate.
Lighting
## Night club lighting, lasers and rave visuals
Lighting is what turns a dark room into a night. Moving heads over the floor, strobes and blinders for the drop, washes to color the whole space and haze so every beam has a shape in the air. We program it to the set so the hits land on the beat all night.
Rave visuals go on the wall behind the booth or across the room: projection, LED content, mapped surfaces, and a VJ running it live with the music. If the DJ brings their own show content we will take it as a source and run it. Event lighting services and projection and video are quoted alongside the audio rather than as a separate booking.
Lasers and cold sparks land inside a club night better than almost anything else, and they carry rules. We quote these only after the venue and, where required, the fire department have approved them. Haze is the same conversation with a smaller sign off, and we confirm it before the date so it runs from doors.

## Rave and night club AV questions

How much sound does a rave need compared to a normal party?

Do you supply a rave DJ, or only the equipment?

Sound Quality
## Four things that decide how a private room sounds
Sound quality at a luxury event comes down to four things: how evenly the room is covered, what the low end does, whether speech stays clear, and how much headroom the system has left when the night gets loud. Here is how we handle each one.
### Even coverage The same sound wherever a guest stands
How 165° horizontal and vertical per panel · line array column
A common complaint about sound quality at a private event is that the room has a loud half and a quiet half. It happens because a conventional cabinet throws a narrow vertical pattern, so a guest standing near the speaker gets more level and more top end than a guest at the far wall, and turning the system up for the far wall punishes everyone near it.
A DML500 panel covers 165 degrees horizontally and 165 degrees vertically, and several panels hung as a line array behave as one tall source, so level falls off gently down the length of the room. A guest at the bar and a guest by the window hear close to the same thing, and people can talk at a normal volume anywhere in the space.
### Low end you can hear as pitch A bass note, played at the right level
How BassBoss ZV28 · flat to 23 Hz ±3 dB · tuned to the room
Plenty of systems are loud underneath and still miss, because the bass arrives as one wide thump rather than as the note that was played. A subwoofer that rolls off early ends up working above its range, and it starts adding its own character to everything below the vocal.
The ZV28 runs flat down to 23 Hz ±3 dB, which is below the lowest note on a five string bass, and it holds that at a level where a typical cabinet has already turned into a rumble. On a listening party or a producer playback session you hear it on a single sustained sub line: the pitch moves, and you can follow it.
### Speech that stays clear Every word from the podium to the back table
How Diffuse wavefront · AI-powered De-Feedback · levels set at the mic position
A luxury venue is usually built out of stone, glass and polished plaster, and those surfaces send sound straight back into the room. Speech is where that shows up first, because the reflection arrives a moment behind the direct sound and smears the consonants that carry the meaning.
Flat panels put less energy into those surfaces to begin with, which is where intelligibility in a hard room starts. The De-Feedback system holds down the frequencies that want to ring, and our engineer sets the level for every microphone with somebody standing at the speaking position before doors. A toast reaches the back table while the system still sounds quiet in the middle of the room.
### Headroom and room tuning Loud with the system working comfortably
How Rig sized above what the room needs · measured and tuned before doors
A system running near its limit sounds tense long before it sounds distorted. The top end hardens, the low end compresses, and a room that felt good at dinner gets tiring two hours later. We size the rig above what the room needs so it spends the night with headroom in hand.
Then it gets tuned to the space it is standing in. Our engineer measures the room, corrects for what the surfaces are doing rather than for how the speaker measures in a warehouse, and sets the system up so it moves from conversation level to full playback in one move with the character staying the same.
The System
## A DML500 line array over BassBoss ZV28 subwoofers, tuned for a private room
One sound system, built for luxury events where the audio has to be full range and the hardware has to stay out of the sightline. Here is what goes in the room and why each piece is in there.
01
### Flat Panel Audio DML500 panels in a line array
Tops Bending wave DML · carbon fiber and Nomex honeycomb · 165 degrees horizontal and vertical
The DML500 is a bending wave panel rather than a cone speaker. A stiff carbon fiber and Nomex honeycomb panel is driven by four neodymium motors, and thousands of small vibrational modes spread across it at once, so the sound leaves as a diffuse wavefront rather than as a beam. Coverage is 165 degrees horizontally and 165 degrees vertically, out of an enclosure thin enough to sit against a wall. A conventional cabinet throws a narrow vertical pattern, so people standing get a different sound from people seated. The panel covers both at once, which is why a room where guests are moving around sounds the same from every spot.
Hung in a line array configuration , several panels work as one tall source. Level drops off more gently with distance than it does from a single point source, so the guests nearest the system stay comfortable while the guests at the far wall still hear everything. In a long room that is the difference between a conversation people can have and a party they have to shout across.
DML500 speaker rental
02
### BassBoss ZV28 subwoofers underneath
Subs Dual 18 inch drivers per cabinet · flat to 23 Hz ±3 dB · ground stacked out of sightline
Panels are a mid and high device, so the low end comes from the subwoofers. The BassBoss ZV28 carries two 18 inch drivers in one cabinet and runs flat down to 23 Hz ±3 dB. That is below the lowest note on a five string bass, so a synth sub or a kick drum arrives as a pitch you can hear rather than as a thump in your chest, and the cabinet holds that at a level where a typical sub has already turned into a rumble. On a listening party or a producer playback session that control is the whole point, because a bass note has to read as a note rather than as pressure.
The cabinets go on the floor, usually tucked against a wall or behind something structural, so the one part of the rig on view is the part guests walk past.
03
### Shure wireless microphones with De-Feedback
Mics Shure wireless handhelds and lapels · AI-powered De-Feedback
Every private event has a moment where somebody talks: a host, a producer introducing a record, an artist thanking a room. We bring Shure wireless handhelds and lapel microphones, and they run through our AI-powered De-Feedback system, which finds and holds down the frequency that is about to ring before it becomes a squeal. That matters more in a luxury venue than in a ballroom, because the marble and glass that make the room look expensive are the same surfaces that make it ring.
The panels help here before the De-Feedback system does anything. A flat panel radiates diffusely instead of aiming a lobe of energy back down the room at an open microphone, so the rig starts with a lot of gain before feedback, and the De-Feedback system takes care of what is left. Between the two the system is feedback resistant enough that the room is ready as placed, with the ringing out already done by the system.
We put fresh batteries in on our own schedule, and we set the level for every microphone with a person standing where the speaker will stand.
Microphone rentals
04
### An audio engineer for the length of the event
Crew One engineer on site · tuned before doors · stays through the night
The rig arrives with the person who knows it. Our audio engineer measures the room, tunes the system against what the surfaces are doing, sets levels with somebody standing at the microphone position, and then stays for the event. If the DJ hands off to a live set, or a producer wants to play a mix at reference level and then drop it back down for conversation, there is somebody at the console to do it in one move.

### Listening parties Album and single playback

A listening party lives or dies on whether the record sounds the way the artist heard it in the studio. Panels are placed so the room reads evenly from wherever a guest is standing, which is the tricky part of a listening event: everyone stays on their feet, and the crowd moves between tracks.

A private DJ set in a home, a penthouse or a members club needs a system that feels like a club at a volume that will not get the building called. Rig DML500 line array · 2 ZV28 subs · multiple source inputs
Producer sessions bring a room full of people who listen for a living, which is the toughest audience a rental system gets. Several sources can be patched at once, so a laptop, an interface and a turntable all go through the same tuned system, patched before the first guest arrives.
### Intimate live sets Acoustic, duo and small band
Rig DML500 line array · 2 ZV28 subs · input list and monitoring
A stripped back performance in a private room is a real live sound job in a space far smaller than a venue. ### Private galas and receptions Speeches, then a floor
Rig DML500 line array · 2 ZV28 subs · handhelds and a lapel
A private gala runs two shows in one night. During dinner and speeches the priority is that every word carries to the back table, which is where the panel coverage and the De-Feedback system earn their place. After the program the same rig turns into a dance system with the subwoofers brought up, so the changeover happens inside the rig, out of sight.
### Brand and press events Launches under embargo
Rig DML500 line array · 2 ZV28 subs · podium mic and press feed
An embargoed launch has the same discretion requirements as a private party and a harder audio brief, because what is said at the podium has to be captured cleanly as well as heard in the room. We provide a clean feed for whoever is recording, run the podium and handheld microphones through the same feedback control, and keep the system out of the camera frame your team is working in.

The cloud is water vapor chilled by carbon dioxide. It stays low, at about ankle to knee height. The machine is quiet while it runs, the cloud has no smell, and it clears quickly.

## Live sound services for every kind of event
Event sound is judged on two things: whether people can hear the words, and whether the music has enough weight to move a room. Those pull in opposite directions, and the equipment that gets one right needs a person watching both to get the other right too. That is the part of live sound services that gets skipped when audio is treated as a delivery. Providing sound for events means holding both at once, all night.
A wedding needs a vow heard from the back row of a garden and then a dance floor that feels like one. A conference needs a panel of four to sound like four separate voices, at the same level, for ninety minutes. A band needs monitors on stage that let the drummer hear the vocalist. We size and tune the system for whichever of those you are running, and we say so in the quote instead of listing a package tier.

Cable runs that survive four hundred people walking over them. A spare handheld already turned on and sitting next to the mixer.

FAQ
## Event audio services questions
What does an audio visual company do for an event?
We supply the equipment and, when the event calls for it, the people who run it. For a typical event that means speakers, microphones, a mixer and playback, plus projection, lighting or a live stream if the event needs them, all delivered to the venue, built inside the load-in window, tuned to the room and sound checked, then operated live by our own engineer or handed to your DJ or mixing engineer, whichever suits the event. At the end we strike it and take it away. You are hiring a service that happens to include equipment, rather than equipment that happens to arrive.
What is included in full-service event audio?
Delivery, setup, tuning, a sound check and strike afterward, all in one quote, with an on-site technician for the event when you book one. We build the system, run and dress the cabling, line-check every input, set the microphone levels and tune the room before guests arrive. For complex setups we recommend an engineer on it for the whole event, and if your DJ or your own mixing engineer is running the system, we sound check with them and come back after the event. Your team does not touch a cable at any point.
Do you provide an on-site sound engineer?
Yes, on request, and we recommend one for complex setups. A technician runs your audio live: microphone levels, music, transitions between segments and the handoffs from a speech to a band to a DJ. For larger events we add a monitor engineer, a stage hand for microphone changes and a lighting operator. The person who tuned the system in the afternoon is the person behind it in the evening. If your DJ or your own mixing engineer is running the system, we set it up, sound check with them and come back after the event.
Can you handle weddings and corporate events?
Yes, and they are most of our calendar. For weddings we cover the ceremony, cocktail hour and reception, often across two or three spaces set in one visit. For corporate events we provide microphones, speakers, program audio and mixing for meetings, panels, general sessions, product launches and galas, with a clean feed out for recording or streaming.
Do you offer live sound for bands?
Yes. Mains, stage monitors, a console sized to the input list, microphones for drums, amps, acoustic instruments and vocals, and a front-of-house engineer for the set. Send us the band's stage plot and input list with your inquiry and we will build the system around it rather than around a package tier.
Do you rent audio visual equipment, or only provide services?
Both, and they are the same inventory. Some clients book us as a production company for the whole event, others just need a sound system for an afternoon. Either way we deliver it, set it up and tune it. Delivery, setup and testing are included, and every system arrives built. Whether our technician then stays on the system or hands it over to your own DJ is the part that changes. Equipment rentals have their own page at sound and AV equipment rental, and the full equipment list names every category we carry.
Do you do audio visual installation?
No. Permanent installed systems, building integration and AV consulting for a fixed room are a different trade with different licensing, and we leave those to the firms that do them full time. We are an event company: we bring the system to your venue, set it up and sound check it for the event, and take it away. If you need a permanent install we are happy to point you toward someone who does it properly.
Can you work with the sound system our venue already has?
Sometimes, and we will tell you honestly which case you are in. House systems in hotels and civic halls are often built for background music and paging rather than for a live event, so a microphone through them will be intelligible but thin. Where the house system is genuinely good we will use it and bring only what it lacks. Where it is not, we bring our own and leave theirs switched off.
How far ahead should I book event sound services?
For a Saturday in wedding season, two to six months is normal and the good dates go first. For corporate work a few weeks is usually fine. We do take short-notice bookings when the equipment and a crew are free, so it is always worth asking, even the same week. Send the date and we will tell you straight away whether we have it.
What areas of Dallas-Fort Worth do you serve?
The whole metroplex, roughly a forty-mile radius from our base in ZIP 76053: Dallas, Fort Worth, Plano, Frisco, Arlington, Irving, Southlake, McKinney, Denton, Grapevine, Richardson, Garland and everywhere in between. If your venue is further out, ask anyway and we will tell you honestly whether it works.

Budgeting
## What sound & AV equipment rental costs in Dallas
Every quote is built for the room, and it is worth explaining why. A published range that runs from a two-speaker party rig to a festival line array is technically true and completely useless. It misprices both ends and says little about yours.
What we can do is tell you what moves the number, so you can size your own budget before you ever speak to us. Four things account for nearly all of it.
### Factor oneGuest count and room volume
Room volume drives the size of the system more than head count does. A hundred and fifty people in a low-ceilinged private room needs a fraction of the system that the same hundred and fifty need in a converted warehouse with thirty-foot ceilings and concrete everywhere. Tall, hard, reverberant rooms are a common reason a system gets bigger.
### Factor twoHow many spaces need audio
A wedding is usually three audio events, not one: a ceremony outside, cocktails somewhere else, a reception in the ballroom. Each space needs its own coverage. A corporate event with breakout rooms works the same way. One room is one system; three rooms is closer to three.
### Factor threeWhat has to happen through the system
Background music is the cheap end. Speeches with wireless microphones, a live band with a full input list, a DJ with real low end, video playback with synchronized audio and a hybrid stream all stack inputs, outputs and hours on top of each other. Tell us the run of show and the number tightens fast.
### Factor fourAccess, timing and the venue
A ground-floor load-in with a dock at two in the afternoon and a fourth-floor ballroom with one service elevator and a ninety-minute turn between events are two different jobs. Distance from Dallas-Fort Worth, union rules, power availability and required certificates of insurance all sit here too.
### The quote includes the parts other quotes add later
Delivery, setup, tuning and strike are in the number we send you, along with an on-site technician if you would like one. Send the date, the venue and roughly how many guests and you will have an itemized quote back within 24 hours. Ask for one here and we will send you a straightforward quote within 24 hours.

Microphone Rental Dallas
## Wireless microphone rental, with the feedback handled.
If you have searched for wireless microphone rental near me, you have probably also sat through the moment a microphone finds its frequency and the whole room flinches. That moment is a predictable interaction between a microphone, a speaker and a room, and it is solvable.
Every microphone we rent runs through our AI-powered De-Feedback system. It listens continuously to what is coming back into the microphone, identifies the narrow frequencies that are about to ring, and pulls them down before they become audible, so a speaker can walk in front of the speakers, a bride can hold a microphone at arm's length, and everyone stands wherever they like.
We rent handheld microphones for toasts and Q&A, lapel microphones for officiants and presenters who need their hands, and podium microphones for anything with a lectern, plus the antenna distribution and frequency coordination that keep a dozen channels from stepping on each other in a crowded building. Full detail on feedback-free microphone rentals .

The short version
## What is a line array PA system?
A line array is a column of matched cabinets stacked in a vertical line so their outputs couple into one source instead of fighting each other. A traditional point-source system loses about 6 dB every time you double the distance from the speaker, which is why the front rows get blasted and the back of the room gets mush. A line array cuts that loss across its usable range, so the first row and the last row hear something much closer to the same thing.
The column is aimed as a unit, at the audience and away from the ceiling, the back wall and the glass. In a reflective venue such as a gymnasium, an atrium or a hard-surfaced ballroom, that directivity is what keeps a presenter intelligible instead of washing the room in reflections.
The working rule we use: below about 250 guests in a normal room, a point-source PA is the right tool. Above that, or outdoors, or in a long room, an array is what keeps every seat sounding the same.
Large format PA
## PA system rental in DFW when two speakers will not cover the room
Also called Public address system · PA rental · large format sound system
Most PA system rental searches in Dallas-Fort Worth end at a pair of powered tops on sticks, and for a lot of events that is the correct answer. The calls that come to this page are the other ones: a general session for 900 where the CEO has to be understood in the back row, a festival stage where the sound has to carry past the barricade, a gymnasium where the last graduation turned into an echo.
The difference goes beyond volume. A bigger point-source system played louder makes the front rows uncomfortable before it makes the back rows clear. An array changes the shape of the coverage rather than the amount of it, which is why we reach for one as soon as the room gets long, tall or full.
If you are still deciding which side of that line your event sits on, send us the venue name and the headcount. ## The BassBoss DV12 array we rent
Rig BassBoss DV12 tops · up to 2 per side · stands to 13 feet

## Concert sound system rental and festival stage sound in Dallas-Fort Worth
Concert and festival work is what a line array was built for. Whether the stage is a festival deck in a field or a theater proscenium, the array is what carries the show past the first twenty rows. These are the four situations we get called for most, and what changes about the rig in each one.
### Outdoor stages in the open air
On an outdoor stage the rig has to do all the work on its own. ### The sub array grows outdoors
A crowd absorbs low end and a field lets the rest roll away, so an outdoor show gets more subwoofers than the same head count indoors. ### Delay towers and front fill
Past a certain depth from the stage, one pair of mains serves the front better than the back. Delay towers put a second source further into the crowd, time aligned so it reinforces the main array instead of smearing it, and front fill covers the guests standing closer than the array is aimed. Both are how a big field stays even.
### Multiple acts sharing one rig
Support acts, a changeover and a headliner all play through the same array, and the array stays where it was tuned. Our engineer holds the system at the level the room was set for across the whole bill, so the last act on stage gets the same coverage the first one had.

## How many subwoofers does your event need?
This is the question almost everyone asks first, and the honest answer starts with three things: how many people are in the room, what the music is, and whether there are walls. A hundred guests in a hotel ballroom and a hundred guests in an open backyard need different amounts of low end, because a ballroom keeps the bass and a backyard gives it away. Below is how we size a rig in practice. Tell us the venue and the guest count and we will tell you which line you are on.
### Up to 100 guestsBackyard, small hall, house party
Rig 1 sub · 2 tops on poles · one 20 amp circuit
One single 18 inch sub under a pair of tops covers a room this size with room to spare. A single sub also keeps the load in small, which matters in a backyard where everything crosses a lawn. The trap at this size is the opposite of what people expect: it is rarely too little bass, it is a rig set too loud for a small space, which is why we set the level with someone standing at the far end of the room rather than at the mixer.
### 100 to 250 guestsBallroom, brewery, larger reception
Rig 2 subs · 2 to 4 tops · separate power for the subs
Two subs is the size most DFW receptions and corporate parties land on. Running a pair rather than one is about more than output. Two boxes placed together couple, which means the low end gets deeper and more even across the dance floor instead of loud in one spot and thin in another. This is also the point where the subs want their own circuit, and we advance that with the venue before the date rather than finding out at load in.
### 250 to 500 guestsClub night, band show, university event
Rig 2 to 4 subs · 4 tops or a small array · dedicated power drop
At this size the room is usually loud enough that the bass has to work through a crowd, and bodies absorb low end. Four subs across the front of a stage give a deep, even field rather than a hot spot in the middle. If the room is long, this is also where we start talking about where the tops go, because a typical pole mount reaches its limit once the vocal at the back has to compete with the kick.
### 500 guests and upFestival, warehouse, outdoor stage
Rig 4 or more subs · line array tops · distro and a generator plan
Outdoors the low end rolls away into open air, so the number of boxes goes up quickly and the arrangement matters as much as the count. Under a covered pavilion this year, open on every side, a pair of DV12s built for outdoor use held a wedding dance floor full to the last song. Subs can be stacked in a block, spread across the stage front or arranged so the bass stays on the crowd and off the neighbors. That last one comes up more than people think in Dallas, and it is worth planning before a noise complaint plans it for you. Larger events also move to line array speakers on top.
### Bass heavy genresEDM, dubstep, drum and bass, rap and hip hop
Rig Add one sub per two tops · or step up a box size
Guest count is only half the sizing question. A jazz trio and a dubstep set with the same hundred people in the room want very different low end, because in one the bass supports the music and in the other the bass is the music. For those genres we either add subs or move to a bigger box rather than pushing a small rig harder, since a sub that is working at its limit stops sounding deep and starts sounding compressed. What those genres want is impact that stays clean at level, rather than a small rig pushed harder.
### Not sure which line you are on?
Send us the venue name, the date and a rough head count. We know most DFW rooms, and for a new one we will ask you for two photos and tell you honestly what it needs. That intake takes about five minutes and it is what makes the rig fit the room.
